body: I think this problem has high priority. Many new PRs are reported as failing now.

The only "solution" I can think of is conditionally (?) skipping the mldata tests.
Or catching the 500 there?
I do not know the issue quite well just a naive question: Can we just cache the data somewhere on travis rather than require it every time?

> The only "solution" I can think of is conditionally (?) skipping the mldata tests.

+1 

How would you achieve that?

> The only "solution" I can think of is conditionally (?) skipping the mldata tests.

+1 we probably need to disable those tests by default and only enable them if a environment variable such as `export SKLEARN_FETCH_TEST_DATA=1` is defined in the test environment.

For doctests this can be done using `_fixture.py` as already done here:

https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/master/doc/datasets/labeled_faces_fixture.py

https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/master/doc/datasets/twenty_newsgroups_fixture.py

Alternatively we could `try` to fetch something from mldata in the fixture and skip the tests if it fails.
We just got bitten by the amg tests not being done on the bots so I'd rather avoid disabling tests by default.

Downloading those datasets potentially hundreds of times per day seems like an awful waste of everyone bandwidth. Unless we find a way to cache it on travis-side I would rather not download it.

We still have jenkins that tests the master branch and were we can cache data and run those dataset dependent tests without any issue.
The  environment variable stuff can be made work the other way around though (to run the tests by default while allowing to explicitly skip them on travis).
+1 for running by default (including jenkins) and skipping on travis.

issue.title: Add fit_transform to FeatureUnion
issue.body:
Implements #1426.

The current implementation requires that all transformers implement `fit_transform`. I believe all transformers in the scikit implement it, either directly or through the `TransformerMixin`. Is it ok to require its presence or should we check for its existence and call `fit` followed by `transform` if it's not present?

`FeatureUnion.transform` and `FeatureUnion.fit_transform`, and also `_transform_one` and `_fit_transform_one` share similar logic, which led to some code duplication.

Let me know if you prefer to factor out common parts at the expense of extra function calls.

I believe this addition is already covered by the test `test_pipeline#test_feature_union`. If you think additional test cases are needed, tell me which.
